diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Recall $\Delta_{1}(1)=1$ and $\Delta_{\ell}(1)=0$ for $\ell\neq1$
because the Gauss--Hermite rule integrates constant functions exactly.

issues.failure_explanation: The witness need not vanish at all sparse-grid nodes: its quadrature value vanishes through the particular Smolyak cancellations. For d=2, L=3, n_1=1 and n_2=2, the grid includes nodes with first coordinate zero, where p_2(0)=4^{-α}>0. Moving weight from a node where the witness vanishes to such a node destroys the cancellation, even if the total weight remains one. Thus the proof does not establish the asserted lower bound for arbitrary weights on the full node set.

failure_location.quote: The lower bound is obtained by exploiting the structure of the Gauss--Hermite nodes and is independent of the quadrature weights; consequently, no modification of the weights can improve the rate $N^{-\alpha/2}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Limit the conclusion to the Smolyak functional actually analyzed. Retaining arbitrary reweighting requires a new lower-bound argument using the entire sampling set, rather than the one-dimensional marginal cancellation.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised impossibility of improving the rate by reweighting is unsupported; the formal lower bounds concern the specified Smolyak functional.
issues.title: The lower-bound argument does not cover arbitrary reweighting
issues.why_classification: The source-supported restriction removes the advertised all-weights impossibility guarantee; retaining that central quantifier requires a different full-node-set lower-bound argument.

issues.failure_explanation: For d>1, the paper's isotropic lower bound includes a growing logarithmic factor, so it is incompatible with a uniform O(N^{-α/2}) worst-case bound. The established upper bound also includes a logarithmic factor. Unlike surrounding statements about the dominant polynomial rate, this sentence makes an unqualified big-O assertion.

failure_location.quote:
the sparse-grid Gauss--Hermite
rule achieves the convergence rate $O(N^{-\alpha/2})$;

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the explicit logarithmic upper bound, or qualify the asserted polynomial rate as holding only up to logarithmic factors.
issues.overall_effect: The introduction advertises a stronger sparse-grid convergence guarantee than the formal results provide.
issues.title: The introduction promises a log-free sparse-grid rate
issues.why_classification: A limited weakening of the advertised rate resolves the problem without changing the analysis, but the strict log-free big-O guarantee cannot be retained.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Suppose that a finite index set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{N}^{d}$ is
downward-closed in one direction.

issues.failure_explanation: The definition is vacuously satisfied when the selected coordinate axis contains no index of Λ. For example, Λ={(2,2)} satisfies the stated condition but has no index (ℓ,1), so the asserted terminal level and ensuing witness are undefined. The empty index set is also admitted and gives N=0, for which the displayed negative power of N is undefined.

failure_location.quote:
Then, for some $\overline{\ell}_{1}\in\mathbb{N}$
we have $(\ell_{1},1\dots,1)\in\Lambda$ for all $\ell_{1}=1,\dots,\overline{\ell}_{1}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Handle an empty selected axis separately using f=1, since the corresponding Smolyak operator annihilates constants. Require N≥1, or use max(1,N) in the bound for the zero-cost case.
issues.overall_effect: The general quadrature and interpolation proofs omit admissible index sets, and their stated bounds need a convention or exclusion for zero evaluations.
issues.title: Directional downward closure does not ensure a nonempty axis
issues.why_classification: A constant-function argument and a zero-cost convention cover the omitted cases while preserving all nontrivial rates and dimension dependence.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Let $n:=n_{\overline{\ell}_{1}}$ denote the number of quadrature
points used in the univariate Gauss--Hermite rule $Q_{\overline{\ell}_{1}}^{\mathrm{uni}}$,
and let $\xi_{1},\dots,\xi_{n}$ be the roots of the univariate Hermite
polynomial $H_{n}$ of degree $n$.

issues.failure_explanation: The hypotheses allow n=1, for example d=1, Λ={1}, n_1=1. Even after the evident correction restricting the gap index to successive roots, there are no such gaps for one root, so p_1 is zero and the proof divides by a zero Sobolev norm. The asserted positive witness quotient therefore does not cover this case.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Treat the one-node Gauss--Hermite rule separately, for example with the witness x_1^2, and decrease the lower-bound constant if necessary.
issues.overall_effect: The witness-based lower bounds lack the permitted one-node case; the isotropic theorem permits it when d=1.
issues.title: The gap witness degenerates for a one-node rule
issues.why_classification: A fixed polynomial witness supplies the missing case without changing any rate, construction for larger n, or dimension-independent constant claim.

issues.failure_explanation: Adding signed quadrature terms can cancel sampling functionals. Take d=2, Λ={(1,1),(1,2)}, n_1=2 and n_2=1, all allowed here. The selected-axis subsum is Q_1⊗Q_1 and has four active nodes, whereas the full operator telescopes to Q_1⊗Q_2 and has two. Thus the displayed comparison would assert 4≤2. The needed conclusion n≤N is true, but not for the reason given.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the already available marginal identity S_Λ(g(x_1))=Q_barℓ(g) for arbitrary univariate g. Since the Gauss--Hermite weights are nonzero, every one of its n nodes must occur among the first-coordinate projections of the active samples, proving N≥n directly.
issues.overall_effect: The conversion of the univariate lower bound to an evaluation-count lower bound has an invalid cost argument.
issues.title: Sampling cost is not monotone under adding Smolyak terms
issues.why_classification: A short marginal-support argument replaces the false monotonicity step and preserves the complete lower-bound statement.

issues.failure_explanation: The sum counts tensor-grid work with multiplicity, not the active sampling points of the resulting quadrature. Already for d=1, L=2, n_1=1 and n_2=2, with M=2 and M_0=1, S_Λ=Q_2 uses two nodes but the asserted sum is three. In higher dimensions both Smolyak cancellations and shared Gauss--Hermite nodes must be accounted for. An upper work bound alone does not establish the lower node-count estimate needed to introduce the logarithmic factor.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Explicitly formulate the result for the multiplicity-counted cost of an implementation that evaluates every tensor grid, including subsequently cancelled work. To retain the claim for distinct active nodes, supply a separate two-sided node-counting argument; merely changing the equality to an upper bound is insufficient.
issues.overall_effect: The logarithmically strengthened lower bounds are not established in terms of the actual active evaluation count.
issues.title: The isotropic node-count identity ignores cancellations and overlap
issues.why_classification: A substantive cost-contract restriction gives a source-supported version, while preserving the original node-count guarantee requires a contained but nontrivial counting argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated size condition does not imply the intervening inequality. For d=4 and n=21, one has 21≥e^3 but (ln 21)^3>21. Consequently this step does not justify the claimed logarithmic comparison, independently of the node-counting issue.

failure_location.quote:
Since $n_{L-d+1}\ge \mathrm{e}^{d-1}$ we have
$(\ln n_{L-d+1})^{d-1}\le n_{L-d+1}$, thus $\ln N\lesssim_{d}2\ln n_{L-d+1}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Once the appropriate counting comparison is established, take logarithms directly: ln N≤C+ln n+(d−1)ln ln n, and bound this by a dimension-dependent multiple of ln n, treating the trivial small cases separately.
issues.overall_effect: The logarithmic conversion in the isotropic quadrature and interpolation lower bounds has an invalid inference.
issues.title: The logarithmic comparison uses a false elementary inequality
issues.why_classification: A routine logarithmic estimate preserves the desired comparison and every stated rate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
where $\mathscr{I}_{\ell}^{\mathrm{uni}}$ is the polynomial interpolation
operator using the zeros of $H_{n_{\ell}+1}$.

and let $\xi_{1},\dots,\xi_{n}$ be the roots of the univariate Hermite
polynomial $H_{n}$ of degree $n$.

issues.failure_explanation: Integrating this interpolant gives the (n_ℓ+1)-point Gauss--Hermite rule, not the n_ℓ-point rule used in the equality. Being interpolatory does not identify quadrature functionals on different nodes. For n=2 and α=1, the defined witness satisfies Q_2(p_2)=0, whereas its interpolant at the three roots of H_3 has Gaussian integral 1/6.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the stated interpolation construction, but use p_{n_barℓ+1} and the matching (n_barℓ+1)-point Gauss--Hermite functional throughout. Adjust the evaluation counts and growth constants accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed comparison with the already established univariate quadrature error does not prove either interpolation lower bound as written.
issues.title: The interpolation proof pairs different Gauss--Hermite node sets
issues.why_classification: Matching the witness and quadrature to the existing interpolation nodes is a local repair, and replacing n by n+1 preserves both rates.

issues.failure_explanation: No lower restriction on L is stated. Taking d=3 and L=1 makes the index set empty, so S_Λ=0 and its worst-case error is one, witnessed by f=1. But the proposed right-hand side is zero because binom(1,2)=0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the estimate for L≥d and handle L<d separately with e(S_Λ)=1.
issues.overall_effect: The general Smolyak proposition is false for permitted low levels, although its later application uses L≥d+1.
issues.title: The Smolyak upper bound omits the level restriction
issues.why_classification: A standard level condition and an explicit zero-grid case preserve every subsequent rate and application.

issues.failure_explanation: All samples lie in [-b,b]^d, and this radius cannot make the worst-case omitted tail as small as N^{-α}. In d=1, take a nonnegative smooth bump f_b(x)=ψ(b(x−b)) supported in (b,b+1/b). Its quadrature value is zero, while I(f_b)/||f_b|| is comparable to exp(−b^2/4)b^{−α−1/2}. With the specified b this is N^{-α/8} times a logarithmic factor, contradicting the claimed N^{-α} bound regardless of the generating vector.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rebalance truncation and periodization using the proved Gaussian decay bound, choosing a sufficiently large constant B in b=B√ln N for a fixed ε∈(0,1/2), and verify the resulting error estimates. The √ln N scaling can be retained.
issues.overall_effect: The affine rank-1 lattice guarantee and the corresponding summary row fail for the prescribed algorithm. The decay embeddings proved within the proposition are not defeated by this counterexample.
issues.title: The affine lattice truncation radius is too small
issues.why_classification: A contained reoptimization of the truncation radius is necessary, but the source's decay estimates support retaining the method and the advertised polynomial and logarithmic orders.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Now, for suitably designed generating matrices $C_{1},\ldots,C_{d}\in\ZZ_{p}^{\NN\times m}$,
a digital net consisting of $N=p^{m}$ points is given by

are given by a higher-order net of order $(2\alpha+1)$ with $N=p^{m}$
elements.

issues.failure_explanation: The common digital-net input specification supplies no quantitative quality bound independent of m. Higher order alone allows nets with arbitrarily poor quality parameters: leading zero rows can concentrate all N distinct points in a shrinking corner. Such matrices can also be obtained by interlacing correspondingly poor first-order matrices. A fixed smooth Gaussian-Sobolev bump near the origin is then missed by both transformed rules for large N, giving nonvanishing error. Thus neither estimate holds uniformly over the stated class merely from its order.

failure_location.quote:
where points
$(\boldsymbol{t}^{(j)})_{j=1,\dots,N}$ are given by a higher-order
net of order $(2\alpha+1)$ with $N=p^{m}$ elements.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify the bounded-quality digital-net families supplied by the cited results, with quality parameters bounded independently of m, and state the permitted dependence of the constants on those parameters and the base.
issues.overall_effect: Both digital-net guarantees require a stronger input specification than the paper states.
issues.title: Digital-net order alone does not imply uniform error bounds
issues.why_classification: A substantive restriction to quantitatively good net families is needed, but it preserves the advertised attainable rates and does not require new change-of-variables analysis.

issues.failure_explanation: Mere differentiability does not define the coefficients and derivatives used in the recurrence. Already r=1, η=1 requires Φ'' through both C_{2,1} and C'_{1,1}. For example, Φ(t)=|t−1/2|^{3/2} is differentiable but does not have the required second derivative at 1/2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For a recurrence at level r, assume Φ∈C^{r+1}, or explicitly require the derivatives appearing in that instance.
issues.overall_effect: The recurrence lemma is ill-defined under its stated regularity hypothesis. Its subsequent applications use sufficiently smooth maps.
issues.title: The Bell recurrence assumes unavailable higher derivatives
issues.why_classification: A standard local regularity condition repairs the lemma, and every later application already satisfies it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus,  in the implementation of QMC methods using such  points, boundary values may be set to zero.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition does not exclude N=1. Its sole lattice point is then the origin, whose transformed integrand value is set to zero by the boundary convention. Hence Q_1(1)=0 while I(1)=||1||=1. The asserted right-hand side is zero because dα>0 and ln 1=0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require N≥2, or replace ln N by ln(eN) and absorb the one-point case into the constant.
issues.overall_effect: The stated lattice estimate and its summary fail at the one-point input.
issues.title: The Möbius lattice bound fails at N=1
issues.why_classification: A standard small-N convention repairs the boundary case without changing any asymptotic guarantee.
